name: The Easy Way Up
beta: Start to the left of the approach boulder, follow the ramp as it climbs rightward through the gap between the cliff and a boulder, then keep traversing rightward beyond a piton for roughly thirty feet.
overview: Follow a ramp rightward between wall and boulder, then keep traversing rightward beyond a pin for roughly 30 ft.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the left of the approach boulder, which is slimy

name: The Good Book
beta: Sustained crack climbing that stays clean and steep, taking gear up to about 3 inches.
overview: Steep, clean, unrelenting crack climbing, held up as possibly the finest Yosemite crack of its grade.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: The Great Roof
beta: Go easily up to the roof, then pull directly over its lip. On the slab above, a couple more bolts lead to a lowering anchor, or you can continue another fifteen feet up pocketed rock to the summit.
overview: A bolted toprope line with easy climbing to a roof, then a pull over the lip onto a slab and on through pockets.

current.area_walk_in: Hike westward along Saratoga Gap Trail toward the waterfall, but peel off short of it onto Ridge Trail. This heads northwest, under a mile; Billy Goat Rock appears first, with Goat Rock just beyond, both beside the path.
current.descent: rappel from the anchor, or continue 15 ft to the summit

name: The Loo Sanction (aka Mt. Witness)
beta: Begin behind a pine, work up flakes, and clip three bolts set close together to reach a ledge. Then shift right and complete the climb via the neighboring Straight Flush line.
overview: Flakes up to three tight bolts and a ledge, then right to finish up Straight Flush.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: The Love Handles
beta: Begin in the little crack that bends rightward (the first bolt is right below it) and follow six bolts upward along the north side. Past the final bolt, bear leftward onto the shoulder. Medium Friends protect the crack.
overview: A string of severely steep bulges up the north face of a tiered formation, launching from a short curving crack.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the dam, then bear up and left as the path bends round the reservoir, threading a gap in the chaparral and along a faint path to the rock’s base.
current.descent: scramble off behind
current.location: Foot of the north face, where a short crack curving right holds the first bolt

name: The Official Route of the 1984 Olympics
beta: Begin in a scoop and angle rightward, clipping a trio of bolts, to reach a cave holding a fixed pin. Step left there and keep climbing, clipping another bolt or two.
overview: Three bolts carry you rightward into a cave; from there it veers left and continues on a further bolt or a couple more.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: in a hollow roughly 50 ft beyond the easy scramble used for Fractured Fissure

name: The Pillar
beta: Pitch one is closely bolted, with four bolts in about fifty feet. Pitch two relies mostly on cams to 3 inches and ends with three bolts below the anchors.
overview: A two-pitch line that has been heavily cleaned up in recent years. The first pitch is closely bolted, four bolts spread over roughly fifty feet; the second leans mostly on gear and finishes with three bolts below the anchors.

current.detailed_rack: first pitch bolts, second pitch mostly gear to 3 in then three bolts

name: The Popemobile
beta: Four bolts lead up onto a slanting ledge, and a fifth bolt sits on the rounded arete higher up. The route can now be finished straight up.
overview: Four bolts lead to a sloped ledge and a fifth sits higher on the arete. The original party angled off left; a direct finish is gritty with long gaps.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 30 ft right of The Heretic, past the corner on the block's sunward-facing south wall

name: The Troll
beta: Clip two bolts to reach the hard section of the neighboring route and join it there; the second pitch crosses the upper face with a single bolt.
overview: A two-pitch route that merges with a neighboring line at its crux, then crosses an upper face.

current.location: 15 ft right of The Orc

name: The Unnatural Act
beta: A roof problem roughly twenty feet off the deck; the landing is friendlier than typical, and two bolts were added for those who want security.
overview: A much-visited highball roof problem. Two bolts have been put in above it, which many find welcome at roughly 20 feet. Variation grades span 5.10-5.11.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Thrill Hammer
beta: To skip the opening difficulties, a ledge of easy scrambling gives a shorter, gentler first pitch. Taking the summit block directly at the finish is protectable with small cams slotted into the horizontal crack beneath it.
overview: A fun route that splits into either one pitch or two, topping out over a summit block.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the rubble-filled gully with a simple scramble to arrive at the conspicuous corner capped by a small roof, which is Rat Race.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Toto Meets the Bighorn
beta: Starting from the ground, work the cracks in the dark stone hidden behind a spiny bush up to a ledge, then take a grittier crack above onto a pinnacle top fitted with two bolts.
overview: Dark-rock cracks hidden behind a thorny bush reach a ledge; a gritty crack above ends on a small pinnacle with two bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: base of the dome, lower and right of the routes to the top

name: B.S. Special
beta: Begin to the left of a low roof and climb easy ramps toward the right. Where they run out, clip two bolts; broken ground then leads to the higher diagonal crack belonging to Fault Line.
overview: Starts on the left of a low roof and trends rightward up easy ramps. After a couple of bolts, fractured rock continues until the line joins the higher diagonal crack that Fault Line follows.

current.area_walk_in: Scramble the second/third-class gully and ledge band that slants upward to the right between the two formations, which delivers you under the upper tower.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Left of a low roof, where the wall begins

name: Trapeze
beta: Start off boulders and clip a bolt en route to a minor ledge. Four variations leave from there, differing in how they handle the ceiling above.
overview: A single bolt leads to a tiny ledge, past which the route divides into four different ways over the ceiling.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Tree Surgeon
beta: A cut-off tree trunk partway up the crack makes the route easy to identify. The crack is wide enough in places to swallow a climber, so bring gear up to about 3.5 inches.
overview: A crack climb easy to identify by the cut-off stump jutting out partway up. In places the crack seems to gulp the climber.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Prelude
beta: Ascend the corner, going by a fixed piton; once it ends, step upward and rightward, clipping a bolt, and carry on to the summit.
overview: Ascends a prominent left-facing corner, passing a piton already in place, then at the corner's end angles up and rightward past a bolt to finish.

current.area_walk_in: Starting at the High Peaks and Tunnel trail junction, keep going north until the path bends sharply left along the ridge top, just ahead of its drop beside Dragonfly Dome. Another path rises from there toward the south and ends at the hill's summit, which is the dome. Bynum's Spire stands nearby to the southwest in a lovely meadow.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: prominent left-facing corner, on the dome's western side

name: Shut Up And Climb
beta: Climb a chimney, step out to the wall, and clip a bolt as you enter a rightward-slanting crack, which merges with Bisk around the midpoint of that route's opening pitch.
overview: Begins in a short chimney, then steps out across the wall, clips one bolt, and gains a slanting crack that merges with Bisk partway through that route's first pitch.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Turtle Vein
beta: Step off a boulder, climb the wall beside a bolt, step across the crack arriving from your left, then go on up the higher wall with one further bolt, merging with Searching For Strippers close to its finish.
overview: Begins on a boulder and works up a face to a bolt, passes the tip of a crack, then finishes on an upper face. Merges with Searching For Strippers close to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on a boulder a short stretch beyond where Strip Search starts, rightward

name: Ungracious and Inconsiderate
beta: The first pitch passes four bolts, and the second pitch consists of a brief crack finishing at a ledge.
overview: A traditional face and crack line. Clip 4 bolts on the way up.

current.descent: double-rope rappel

name: Baboon Crack
beta: Clip the second bolt of the neighboring route, downclimb, then start this line to the right and angle across past a pre-clipped bolt. One awkward move takes cams, and you then continue to the neighbor's final bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Take the official path that leaves the reservoir and runs northeast to the formation.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Wavelength
beta: An eye-catching finger crack with a single bolt about one-third of the height up.
overview: An eye-catching finger crack splitting the formation's eastern flank. Just one bolt protects it, placed about one-third up, and it is generally toproped.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: A solid top anchor is hard to find.

name: We'll Get Them Little Pricks (aka Cunning Linquist)
beta: Begin in the crack that cuts the south face and climb it, then angle leftward beyond a bolt before returning rightward for the final stretch.
overview: Crack first, then leftward with one bolt, then rightward again to finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: crack on the southern side, 50 ft lower and to the right of Chernobyl Crack

name: Wedlock
beta: Climb the fingercrack until you can bridge across to the chockstone's left flank, then downclimb off it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Eastern wall of the corridor, close to its southern mouth

name: West Face
beta: Pass a shrub and a bolt on the wall to gain a corner, then sidestep right over the wall beyond another bolt to the chimney's foot. Inside the chimney two fixed pitons appear, after which the going eases toward the summit.
overview: A line at the extreme right of the west wall that reaches a corner, then a chimney with fixed pins, and finishes on the summit.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: At the extreme right of the west side

name: Wet T-Shirt Night
beta: Starting from the lower bolts works fine, while the original toprope version entered by moving across a horizontal crack from the right.
overview: Right of Jugline; can start from the lower bolts, whereas the original top-rope start traversed in along a horizontal crack.

current.area_walk_in: From Hidden Valley campground walk north, past the Iron Door Cave area and the east end of The Blob, then aim for the overhanging face across easy boulders to a mostly flat base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: right of Jugline

name: What's It To You
beta: Climb up, then go left in the horizontal to reach a thin crack and follow it to the top. A bolt on a neighboring route can now be used for protection.
overview: A route that starts off a ledge, goes left along a horizontal, and then follows a thin crack to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts off a ledge about 30 ft up and right of the previous route; up, left along a horizontal, then a thin crack to the top

name: When Lightning Strikes
beta: Step off a boulder and head up a four-bolt line; the route veers sharply leftward in the stretch after bolt three.
overview: Bolted line that jogs sharply leftward between its upper bolts; the gap to the first clip is a serious runout.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: from a boulder immediately beyond Born to be a Cowboy on the right

name: When Sheep Ran Scared
beta: Begin like the two routes before it, then angle rightward to a bolt sitting above a horizontal break. Veer leftward until Overpass's slanting crack finishes, then climb vertically past one more bolt to join Overhang Bypass where its opening pitch ends.
overview: Heads rightward to one bolt over a horizontal crack, then leftward to the upper end of Overpass's slanting crack, and straight up beyond another bolt into Overhang Bypass.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts with Underpass and Overpass, then angles rightward to a bolt sitting over a horizontal crack

name: Who Came First
beta: Launch from a boulder tucked behind a tree and go rightward along a dike, clipping a bolt, then straight upward through four further bolts and leftward to a bolted belay. One more bolt, missing its hanger, remains above.
overview: Traverses rightward along a dike with one bolt, rises vertically through four further bolts, cuts left to belay bolts, then continues up-right with one more hangerless bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts from a boulder tucked behind a tree, 40 ft along from Quadrophenia

name: Who Cut The Cheese?
beta: Ascend a groove that turns into a fist crack, beside the bolted chute on its right.
overview: A groove with a fist-sized crack, positioned beside a chute that has bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: low tier, approx. 60 ft beyond the gully

name: Wild Brew Yonder
beta: Three bolts protect a narrow face covered in buckets, and the highest of them is placed well up.
overview: A narrow, bucket-covered face with its third bolt placed well up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: directly beside Fissure Merde

name: Wild Dream
beta: Begin at the wall's left edge and angle rightward across the patina plates toward a pair of bolts near the summit.
overview: Angles rightward over patina plates toward a pair of bolts high on the wall.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: high on the crag north side, on a wall of patina plates

name: Working For Peanuts
beta: Begin beside a conspicuous tree with three trunks, climb leftward to a piton hammered into the arch, then rightward to a bolt. Work upward and leftward, then swing back toward the right to get over the headwall; easier ground leads to a belay with two bolts.
overview: A winding line past an arch and over a headwall, ending at a belay near the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left of a prominent tree with three trunks

name: Youth Run Wild
beta: A crack leads onto a gritty face, which has one bolt.
overview: A crack leads onto a coarse, grainy face with a bolt. The summit anchor is in poor shape and due for replacement.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: bolted rap/belay point in poor condition

name: Yucca Bowl
beta: Go up the gully, move right into a crack, and finish past two bolts.
overview: Ascend the gully, shift right along a crack, and continue past two bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: gully immediately right of True Grit

name: Zygote
beta: On its own separate face, climb to a little pocket and then continue up the wall above, clipping a bolt.
overview: Reach a small pocket, then continue over the face above with one bolt for protection.

current.area_walk_in: A marked footpath runs roughly 250 yards northeast to the formation.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: A Midsummer Night's Dream
beta:
Expect thin fingers on pitch two, where the hardest moves surmount a bulge. Higher up you stem a shallow dihedral and swing out through a roof, then merge with the neighbouring route for the finish.

A regular trad rack of nuts and cams is enough. Pitch one starts mid-ledge, jams up to a slender corner, and gets over a roof with a single 5.9 pull.
overview: Five pitches of jams and corners in fine stone, ending where it meets the last pair of pitches on Leisure Climb. The hardest technical moves come in the thin crack of pitch two.

current.area_walk_in: Almost everyone descends Cruise Gully, entered at a sign on the rim between the campground and the ranger station. It steps down through two rappel sections, often with fixed lines already in place, and lets out on bushy talus at the foot of the wall.
current.location: Follows the steep crack line beside Leisure Climb, starting on the grass shelf, in its centre.

name: Adrenaline
beta:
This is a long, wandering line that weaves across two neighbouring routes and keeps drifting left, so staying on route matters more than any single hard move.

Difficulties are scattered: the runout outer face of a tall corner midway, then a short downclimb of a slim arcing seam to reach a ramp, and finally delicate climbing near the top.
overview: The longest line on Sundance: it starts east of English Opening and wanders leftward across the Eumenides slab for roughly 800 ft.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Black Canyon trail westward, passing under the entire west side of Lumpy Ridge, for two stiff miles. A little cairn flags the spur path, which winds up the steep forested hillside under the buttress and finishes close to an enormous flake propped against Turnkorner Buttress.
current.location: Corner facing left, immediately east of the English Opening line

name: Air Arete
beta: Head up to the little overhang, shuffle rightward onto the low-angle arete, and follow it to the ledge. Bolts here were removed and gear is scarce, so it is best treated as a toprope problem.
overview: Climb to a small roof, traverse right onto a slabby arete and pad up to a ledge with rappel bolts. The protection bolts were removed and gear is scarce, so it is usually toproped.

current.area_walk_in: Find the climbers' trail through the forest and up the steep talus slope, heading for the canyon just right of the main wall. Loose rock is common, so avoid kicking stones down onto others.
current.descent: rappel from the ledge anchors
current.location: Right of Pirouette, below a narrow roof about 15 ft up

name: Air Voyage
beta:
A big ramp is scrambled for a few hundred feet before real climbing starts. The hardest section is a nasty wide crack on pitch 10, and pitch 11 follows with frightening face moves protected by an old bolt.

Carry a generous rack: RPs, nuts, doubles of cams to #4 (three #4s), plus wide-crack protection like big tri-cams or tube chocks. A thin piton may help on pitch 12.
overview: A big 13-pitch line on the southern side of this canyon wall, airy and fairly serious, with plenty of difficult crack climbing and some bold face climbing on the upper pitches.

current.area_walk_in: Almost everyone descends Cruise Gully, entered at a sign on the rim between the campground and the ranger station. It steps down through two rappel sections, often with fixed lines already in place, and lets out on bushy talus at the foot of the wall.
current.detailed_rack: Big rack: RPs, nuts, two sets of cams to #4 with three #4s, wide-crack pieces, and a thin piton for pitch 12.
current.location: west of the Nose's base, about 90 m up the Diagonal ramp where the technical climbing starts
